texts: A stable, pain-free patient with three-vessel disease after an ST-elevation infarction is best served by CABG more than 72 hours after the onset of pain.
Operating within the first days of a transmural infarction carries a clearly higher mortality, so a stable patient waits.
He is diabetic with three-vessel disease and an ejection fraction of 35%, which favours surgery over stenting.
Urgent CABG with a balloon pump is for ongoing ischaemia, shock or mechanical complications, none of which he has.
Six weeks of medical therapy only adds the risk of a new event while waiting.
In the picture, Sanji holds the cabbage crate while the station clock turns, a swimmer and a dragon tattooed on the calm sailor.
Memory hook: a calm sailor in the stable waits for the clock to pass seventy-two.
